prompt:
The charts below show how an average household in one region divided its spending in 2000 and in 2020.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

visual.title: Household spending by category, 2000 and 2020
visual.alt: Two pie charts showing the breakdown of an average household's spending across six categories, for 2000 and 2020.

key_points: The largest category changes hands: food was first in 2000 (30%), while housing is first in 2020 (32%)
Food's share falls from 30% to 19%, an 11-point drop, the largest fall of any category
Housing's share rises from 24% to 32% — the largest increase
Health and education rises from 9% to 14%, making it the fastest-growing category in proportional terms
Transport (14% → 15%) and leisure (11% → 13%) stay almost the same; 'other goods and services' falls from 12% to 7%, becoming the smallest category in 2020
In both years the shares add up to 100%; the charts show distribution, not the amount spent
common_mistakes: Describing the share as if it were an amount ('households spent more money on housing') — the chart only shows distribution
Reading the six slices for each chart in order without highlighting the most striking changes (food and housing)
Overstating categories that barely changed (transport, leisure) as having 'increased'
Adding a reason or recommendation ('housing became too expensive, so…')
